title_short: April · My Kids Are Proud of Me
length: about 2:10 as briefed; about 90 s with the trims in the decision
headline: A peer in Omaha once did not believe she could recover. Now her kids look her in the eye and tell her they are proud of her.
story: April is a peer support specialist in Omaha. On her first day MHA felt almost “sketchy”, because she had never felt an energy like it. With her peers she can be her authentic self, and it feels “like what families should have felt like”. There was a time she did not believe she could recover.
Now hope looks like her kids telling her they are proud of her. It must feel warm, honest and hopeful. Her past is only what she says herself.
do: Open on frame 1 on April talking about her kids. Hook text on frame 1.
Name super after the hook: April Knighton · Peer Support Specialist · MHA Nebraska (spelling confirmed first).
Use the chalk B-roll only where it matches her words. Otherwise stay on her.
Cut the long pauses. Keep her own rhythm.
Hold 1 s after “around you” before the end card.
dont: Her kids are only “my kids”. No names, ages or photos.
Do not use her WRAP answers (04:03–06:02). They are the WRAP promo's material.
“The clinical side” (01:18) is never the point of the video.
Nothing about her family history beyond her own words at 02:33.
No dark music, no slow motion. No second aspect ratio.
